note: Dak Prescott has been on fire as the QB4 in fantasy points per game. Joe Milton could have his fantasy showing of the season this week. Yes, that's not saying much, though. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the tenth-highest passing success rate while ranking 15th in yards per attempt, 17th in EPA per dropback, and 16th in CPOE.

After two starts, Fernando Mendoza looks like the real deal. Last week, he was the QB3 in fantasy scoring. In his previous start, against one of the best pass defenses in the NFL, he was the QB18 for the week. Mendoza is adding something with his legs weekly, with 22 rushing yards in both games and a rushing score. Last week, among 26 qualifying quarterbacks, Mendoza was 12th in yards per attempt, 22nd in catchable target rate, and 21st in highly accurate throw rate. Mendoza will have another tough test this week. He should post at least decent QB2 production. Last week, Cam Ward stacked his third consecutive QB1 outing in a row as the QB5 for the week. The last time that Geno Smith faced this Miami secondary, he chucked it for 289 through the air with 9.3 yards per attempt and three passing scores. Smith was the QB5 for the week with 24.6 fantasy points. Smith could easily be a QB1 this week. Smith has been playing good football this season. Among 32 qualifying passers, Smith is tenth in yards per attempt, 12th in passing success rate, tenth in catchable target rate, and eighth in hero throw rate. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 12th-highest yards per attempt while allowing the 15th-highest passing success rate and CPOE.

Last week was Baker Mayfield's first game of the season with multiple passing touchdowns as the QB11 for the week. Anthony Richardson will be the Colts' starting quarterback moving forward. I feel bad for Michael Penix. A ticked-off Minnesota pass defense is likely to light him up this week like a Christmas tree. Penix is the QB24 in fantasy points per game. Phillips may be worth a look in 32 team DB leagues and 20+ team CB leagues, but should not be a serious consideration for Week 12 elsewhere. Explore alternative options for Week 12.

Tyson Campbell stepped up in Week 10, racking up one solo, four assists, one tackle for loss, one interception, and three passes defended. Tyson is a solid CB2/3 play, but can safely be ignored outside of 32-team DB leagues. Look elsewhere for Week 12.

Rock Ya-Sin stepped up in Week 11, reeling off nine solos and one assist. It was the second spike week of the season for Rock, who has offered CB3 value at best this season. He should not be a consideration in DB leagues for Week 12, even as a flex2, due to zero teams being on bye. Look elsewhere for your Week 12 flex/flex2.

Renardo Green was excellent in Week 11, piling up nine solos. It was the second straight spike week for Renardo, who has forced his way into the CB1/DB4 conversation with his impressive recent stretch. Fire Green up where needed for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Jaylon Johnson heated up in Week 11, recording seven solos. Jaylon has now posted back-to-back spike weeks and should be counted as a top-25 CB option while he is hot. Feel free to look elsewhere in DB leagues.

Josh Jobe stepped up in Week 10, tallying five solos and two tackles for loss. Jobe remains a solid CB2 option, but production like this reminds us that he does indeed have CB1 upside. Fire the Seahawks corner up as a CB2 where needed, but avoid him in DB leagues.

Marcus Epps impressed in Week 11, tallying eight solos and one tackle for loss on 83 percent of the snaps. Epps recorded his first spike week while playing a season high in snaps and should be locked into starters snaps the rest of the way. The Eagles would likely prefer to play him in a more rotational role but with the other safety options failing to step up, Philadelphia should lean on their veteran. Treat Epps as bench depth for Week 12, with an eye on him becoming a DB4/5 option when the byes resume in Week 13.

Ji'Ayir Brown stepped up in Week 11, racking up three solos, one assist, one interception, one pass defended, and one touchdown on 61 percent of the snaps). Brown remains in a fantasy frustrating three man platoon at safety, splitting time with Marques Sigle (70 percent) and Malik Mustapha (73 percent), making him hard to trust week to week. With that said, he does offer some value as a DB4 option during the byes. However, with no byes this week, fantasy managers are advised to look elsewhere for options with higher floors and upside.

Deommodore Lenoir heated up in Week 11, registering three solos, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and two passes defended. Lenoir has put together back to back spike weeks and should be counted as a CB2 option while he's hot. There should not be a reason to start him in DB leagues with no teams on bye, but he can be conadered a DB5 in a pinch.

Paulson Adebo stepped up in Week 11, tallying one solo, one interception, and four passes defended. It was the first spike week of the season for Adebo, who played a season high 93 percent of the snaps one week after being a healthy inactive. Adebo is only back in the stratuing lineup tdue to Greg Newsome being placed on IR, but find himself right back in the DB3/4 mix due to hsi proven upside. Start Adebo where needed for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Indianpolis Colts.

Andre Cisco played just seven percent of the snaps in Week 11 and is back to a strict reserve role with Kerby Joseph healthy. He is worth holding on to in dynasty leagues, but those in redraft leagues should feel free to cut bait altogether, as it will take another injury for Cisco to sniff a fantasy-relevant snap count again this season.
